title: Create form templates and request a client form
summary: Publish clear questions and keep completed forms tied to the wording the client saw.

sections.title: Publish a template
sections.body:
You need form-management permission. Open a client profile, choose **Client records** and expand **Manage form templates**.

1. In **Start or revise**, choose **New template** or an existing template.
2. Enter required **Internal name**, **Purpose** and **Title shown to clients**. **Introduction** and **Associated services** are optional.
3. For each field, enter **Question or wording** and choose **Answer type**. Supported choices include Text, Number, Date, Yes/no, Multiple choice and Signature.
4. For Multiple choice, enter **Choices** one per line. Choose **Required answer** where needed.
5. Use **Add field** or **Remove field** to shape the form.
6. Select **Publish new version**.

A revised version does not rewrite the wording retained with previously completed forms.

sections.title: Request a form for a client
sections.body:
1. In **Client records → Forms and consent**, choose **Form template**.
2. Choose **Originating appointment**, or leave **No appointment link** if this is a general request.
3. Select **Create form link**.
4. Use the secure link shown by the application and share it privately through an appropriate permitted channel. Creating a link alone is not proof that a message was sent.
5. Check the form’s status in **Forms and consent** after the client responds.

The client completes the published form through its private link; they do not need a team login.

sections.title: Read consent carefully
sections.body:
**Consent history** records the type, status and time of captured consent. A completed consultation form is not automatically permission for every kind of communication or use of photographs.

If a private form link expired or no longer permits an answer, return to the client record and create an appropriate new request. Never reuse one person’s form link for someone else.
